one_line: Nayaka ruler of Madurai who rebuilt the capital, expanded the Meenakshi temple-city, and raised Thirumalai Nayakkar Mahal in the 17th century.

appearance.age_look: mid-40s, solid medium-tall build, dignified and energetic
appearance.face: oval face with medium-brown South Indian complexion, sharp nose, neatly trimmed black moustache, faint beard shadow, calm thoughtful eyes with a confident half-smile
appearance.hair: thick black hair pulled back into a tight, high knotted bun at the back of the crown, front kept smooth; adorned with a simple gold circlet-band resting low on the forehead, with a small ruby-like cabochon at the center and no towering crown
appearance.costume: 17th‑century Nayaka royal attire: an off‑white cotton angavastram-style upper cloth draped diagonally from left shoulder across the chest and around the torso, leaving the right shoulder covered and forming soft folds; a rich deep maroon silk dhoti wrapped in the veshti style to ankle length with a broad golden border at the hem and a slightly pleated front; a fitted pale cream long‑sleeved angarkha-like under-tunic visible at neck and wrists beneath the drape; simple open brown leather sandals; jewellery limited to a long, heavy gold chain with a round pendant resting at mid-chest, a shorter necklace of small gold beads, two slim gold bangles on each wrist, and a pair of small round gold earrings.
appearance.signature: a rolled architectural palm‑leaf manuscript tied with a thin red cord in his left hand and a short wooden measuring staff tucked under his right arm, symbolizing his planning of Madurai’s processional streets and palace arches.

ref_desc: Tirumala Nayaka appears as a mid‑40s South Indian ruler with an oval medium‑brown face, black hair in a high bun and gold circlet, off‑white draped upper cloth, cream tunic, deep maroon gold‑bordered dhoti, simple jewellery, sandals, and a palm‑leaf plan scroll with measuring staff, in maroon, gold, off‑white, cream and brown tones.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full‑body anime‑style character model of Tirumala Nayaka standing in a dignified planner’s pose: a mid‑40s South Indian ruler with an oval medium‑brown face, sharp nose, neat black moustache and calm, thoughtful eyes, black hair pulled into a tight high bun at the back of the crown, front smooth, wearing a simple gold circlet-band with a small central ruby-like stone. He is dressed in era-accurate 17th‑century Nayaka royal clothing: an off‑white cotton upper cloth draped diagonally from his left shoulder across his chest and around his torso, covering both shoulders in layered folds; beneath it a pale cream long‑sleeved tunic visible at the collar and cuffs; and a rich deep maroon silk dhoti wrapped veshti‑style down to the ankles with a broad golden border along the hem and soft front pleats. On his feet are plain brown leather sandals. Show his jewellery as a long heavy gold chain with a round pendant at mid-chest, a shorter necklace of small gold beads close to the neck, two slim gold bangles on each wrist, and small round gold stud earrings, avoiding any oversized crown or fantastical ornaments. In his left hand he holds a neatly rolled architectural palm‑leaf manuscript tied with a thin red cord, and under his right arm a short wooden measuring staff, both clearly visible as his signature planning tools. Use a palette dominated by deep maroon, gold, off‑white, cream and brown, and present him from head to toe in a neutral, clear stance suitable for consistent redraws.
